narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Dot-Matrix Manifesto"**

One ink, one typeface, one grid. The page reads like a statement printed in red on cream paper. The dot grid lives in the mark alone: the wordmark and monogram are grids of circles, and the type around them is a narrow editorial grotesk (Cabinet Grotesk), so the mark is the one textured thing on the page. Nothing on the page is decorative. Depth, hierarchy and emphasis all come from size, weight, case and 1px rules, never from a second colour.

The voice is plain-spoken. Sentences are short and declarative, set large, with generous vertical space between them. The system says as little as possible and lets the ink do the work. Interaction follows the same logic: things look printed, then flip like a switch on hover: an outline becomes solid. Nothing fades in, and nothing scrolls: the whole site is one screen.

The user has rejected the crypto-site defaults outright: no glassmorphism or gradients, no dark mode, no stock imagery or 3D, and no colour beyond the two inks.
keyCharacteristics: Two colours only: Signal Red on Cream Paper. No greys, tints or opacity tricks.
One typeface (Cabinet Grotesk) carrying every role from 19px labels to 96px display.
Structure drawn with 1px Signal Red rules that span the full viewport.
Square corners everywhere except the dots themselves, which are perfect circles.
One fixed screen with no scrolling; hover transitions are the only motion.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Everything is Signal Red on Cream Paper. No third colour, no grey, no tint of red, and no opacity used to fake a secondary tone. Hierarchy is the type's job.

rules.name: The Inversion Rule
rules.body: The only permitted colour change is a full swap: red on cream becomes cream on red for a hovered control. Partial fills and mixed states do not exist.

rules.name: The Large Print Rule
rules.body: The pair measures 3.93:1, which passes WCAG AA only for large text. So the palette stays and the type does the work: anything meant to be read is set at WCAG "large" size, 24px or more at a regular weight, or 19px or more in bold (18.66px is the threshold; with Cabinet, bold means 800). No readable text goes below that, at any width.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Cabinet Grotesk only, in two weights (500, 800). Hierarchy is carried by size, weight, case and tracking, never by colour and never by a second family, including monospace for numbers.

rules.name: The Short Line Rule
rules.body: Display and headline copy is one sentence. Measures are capped (headline 16ch, body large 34ch) so lines stay short enough to read as printed statements.

rules.name: The Ruled Sheet Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn, not implied. Bands are separated by 1px Signal Red rules; there are no background panels, cards or containers to group content.

rules.name: The Square Print Rule
rules.body: Corners are square. Circles are reserved for the dot grid; no pill buttons, rounded cards or soft edges.

rules.name: The Switch Rule
rules.body: Hover is a state flip, not a fade. Outline becomes solid. Durations stay at or under 0.45s with the standard ease (cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)); nothing scales up, bounces or glows.

dos: Do set every colour from the two tokens: Signal Red (#E02329) on Cream Paper (#EDEBD6), inverted only for a hovered control.
Do draw structure with 1px Signal Red rules that span the full viewport; they are the only structural lines.
Do render the wordmark and monogram from the circle data in `lib/dots.ts` as SVG so they stay crisp; never rasterise or re-trace them.
Do carry hierarchy with Cabinet Grotesk's size, weight, case and tracking; two weights (500, 800) are enough.
Do keep copy plain-spoken: one sentence per headline, capped measures, no adjectives for their own sake.
Do keep motion to hover: a 0.2s inversion on buttons and an underline on links. Hover styles sit inside `@media (hover: hover)` so a tap never sticks.
donts: Don't use glassmorphism, gradients, glows, blur panels or gradient text.
Don't add a dark mode; Cream Paper is the only background.
Don't use stock imagery, photography, illustrations or 3D shapes.
Don't introduce a third colour, a grey, a tint of red, or opacity used as a tone.
Don't add entrance, scroll or loading animation, or make the page scroll; it is one static screen by decision.
Don't round corners, add cards or background panels, or reach for a second typeface.
